paragraphs.heading: The largest structures known
paragraphs.text: The cosmic web is the network of galaxy filaments that sets the overall shape of the observable universe. Galaxy filaments are the largest structures we know of. Each one is built from walls of superclusters of galaxies.

paragraphs.heading: How big they get
paragraphs.text: These thread-like structures often stretch 50 to 80 megaparsecs, which is 160 to 260 million light-years. The biggest found so far, named Quipu, reaches 400 megaparsecs. An even larger one, the Hercules–Corona Borealis Great Wall, may be around 3 gigaparsecs long, but it is not yet confirmed. Filaments form the borders between voids.

paragraphs.heading: A web that will come apart
paragraphs.text: A filament is made of clusters of galaxies, and each cluster is held together by its own gravity. But the expansion of the universe is speeding up. As a result, those clusters are moving away from one another faster and faster. In the far future, the filaments will break up.

paragraphs.heading: Finding the great walls
paragraphs.text: Astronomers started finding structures bigger than superclusters in the late 1980s. The CfA2 Great Wall was found in 1989, and the Sloan Great Wall followed in 2003. In November 2013, a team used gamma-ray bursts as markers to find the Hercules–Corona Borealis Great Wall, a filament more than 10 billion light-years across.

paragraphs.heading: Two shapes
paragraphs.text: Filaments come in two types. In the filament type, a slice across the structure is roughly as wide in one direction as the other. In the galaxy wall type, that slice is much longer in one direction than the other. Adi Zitrin and Noah Brosch proposed a short filament near the Milky Way and the Local Group, spotted from a line of star-forming galaxies.

paragraphs.heading: Walls close to home
paragraphs.text: A Centaurus Great Wall has been proposed that would include the Virgo Supercluster, also called the Local Supercluster, which holds the Milky Way. Another wall was put forward as the physical form of the Great Attractor, and the Norma Cluster would belong to it. That idea was later replaced by Laniakea, a proposed supercluster taking in the Great Attractor, the Virgo Supercluster and the Hydra–Centaurus Superclusters.

paragraphs.heading: Groups of quasars
paragraphs.text: Large quasar groups, or LQGs, are among the largest known structures too. In January 2013, a team led by Roger Clowes announced one called the Huge-LQG, which is bigger than any galaxy filament found before it. LQGs are thought to be early forms of filaments and of complexes of superclusters.
